items.headline: Income Tax department nudges taxpayers to disclose overseas properties
items.why: The Income Tax department is urging eligible taxpayers to disclose overseas properties and other specified foreign assets under the one-time FAST-DS scheme by 31 December. Qualifying declarations get tax and penalty relief.
implications: Taxpayers who hold foreign assets they have not yet reported face a fixed window in which the relief applies, so the deadline works as a compliance obligation for them.
The scheme could give the tax department fuller information on Indian taxpayers' overseas holdings, and may bring in some additional tax revenue.

exposure.reason: This is a compliance obligation for the limited group of taxpayers who hold foreign assets, not a household essential, so the effect is confined to that group.

horizon.reason: The disclosure window runs until 31 December, roughly two months after the report date, and that deadline sets when taxpayers must act.

confidence.reason: This rests on a single Mint report that cites the Income Tax department's push; the exact eligibility conditions and the size of the relief are not spelled out.

affected.effect: Disclosures of foreign assets under the scheme could add to tax collected and widen the department's information on overseas holdings.

watch.what: The close of the disclosure window under the FAST-DS scheme for specified foreign assets
watch.why: It marks the last date on which qualifying declarations can receive the tax and penalty relief.

context: Indian tax residents are generally taxed on their worldwide income and are expected to report foreign assets to the tax authorities, so undisclosed overseas property can lead to penalties.

terms.meaning: A one-time scheme run by the Income Tax department that lets eligible taxpayers disclose specified foreign assets with tax and penalty relief.

chain.detail: The Income Tax department is nudging taxpayers to disclose overseas properties under the one-time FAST-DS scheme.
Eligible taxpayers can declare specified foreign assets by 31 December and receive tax and penalty relief for qualifying declarations.
Taxpayers who come forward could avoid the full penalties, while the department may gain a clearer picture of Indians' overseas holdings.

impact_chain.breaks_if: The effect would stop if taxpayers do not qualify under the scheme's conditions or do not make a declaration before the 31 December deadline.

reports.headline: Income Tax department nudges taxpayers to disclose overseas properties
reports.summary: Under the one-time FAST-DS scheme, eligible taxpayers can disclose specified foreign assets by 31 December, with tax and penalty relief for qualifying declarations.

items.headline: Supreme Court clarifies scope of police custody under BNSS
items.why: The Supreme Court has held that Section 187(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) enlarges the window in which police may seek custody of an arrested person. This changes how investigators and courts handle custody requests across India.
implications: Investigators may have more room to ask a magistrate for police custody, which could change how long and at what stage an accused person is questioned.
Magistrates and defence lawyers in every state will have to apply the Court's reading when custody applications are argued, so practice that differed between courts may become more uniform.

exposure.reason: The reports describe only a legal clarification on custody procedure. It has no direct channel to household essentials, trade or travel, and reaches people only if they are arrested and investigated.

horizon.reason: A Supreme Court interpretation of the law guides courts as soon as it is delivered, so it can apply to custody requests heard from now on.

confidence.reason: This rests on a single outlet, The Hindu, reporting a Supreme Court holding; the case details and the exact limits of the ruling are not in the report.

affected.effect: Business people facing criminal investigation could see police custody sought over a wider window, although the report does not say that any particular business case is involved.

watch.what: Publication of the full judgment setting out how Section 187(2) of the BNSS is to be applied
watch.why: The detailed reasoning would show how wide the enlarged custody window is and what conditions courts must apply.

watch.what: Trial courts and High Courts citing the ruling when deciding police custody requests
watch.why: This would show whether the clarification changes everyday custody practice for investigators and accused persons.

context: The BNSS is the criminal procedure law that replaced the older Code of Criminal Procedure. Police custody, in which investigators question the accused, is different from judicial custody and needs a magistrate's authorisation within limits set by law.

terms.meaning: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, India's criminal procedure law, which sets out how arrests, custody, investigation and trials are conducted.

chain.detail: The Court held that Section 187(2) of the BNSS enlarges the window during which police custody may be sought. This sets the legal rule that magistrates and investigators must now follow.
The ruling clarifies the scope of police custody under the BNSS, so courts across states can apply one reading when investigators ask for custody of an arrested person.

chain.step: Accused persons may face wider custody requests
chain.detail: Investigators may use the larger window to seek police custody later or in stages. People arrested in any kind of case, including business or financial offences, could therefore be questioned in custody for longer.

impact_chain.breaks_if: The effect would be limited if magistrates refuse custody requests or if the full judgment attaches strict conditions that keep the practical window close to what it was before.

filter.reason: Supreme Court ruling widens the police custody window under BNSS for all cases.

reports.headline: Supreme Court clarifies scope of police custody under BNSS
reports.summary: Court held that Section 187(2) of BNSS enlarges the window during which police custody may be sought

items.headline: Revanth to meet Fadnavis for Tummidihatti project height approval in Mumbai

implications: The Hindu reports that Telangana needs the approved height for the barrage to serve its intended benefits, so the height is central to what the project can deliver.

items.headline: NHAI issues guidelines for upgradation, maintenance, smart monitoring of toilet facilities, parking at National Highway toll plazas
items.why: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued guidelines for toilets and parking at national highway toll plazas. They require an accessible toilet at each covered plaza, citizen feedback by QR code, and fines for agencies that miss standards.
implications: Because agencies face financial penalties, toll plaza operators now have a direct cost for poor upkeep, which could push them to maintain facilities more reliably.
QR code-based feedback lets highway users report poor conditions directly, which could give NHAI a record of complaints for checking compliance.

horizon.reason: Upgrading and maintaining physical facilities at many plazas takes time, so travellers are likely to notice changes gradually rather than immediately.

watch.where: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) official website

context: Toll plaza amenities are usually run by agencies contracted by NHAI, so standards depend largely on how well those contract terms are monitored and enforced.

terms.meaning: A toilet designed so that everyone can use it, including people with disabilities, older people and others with limited mobility.

chain.detail: NHAI has mandated at least one universally accessible toilet at each covered toll plaza, along with smart monitoring, QR code-based citizen feedback and financial penalties for agencies that fail standards.

items.headline: Free travel scheme: Keralam govt. releases ₹88.23 crore to KSRTC to cover revenue loss
items.why: The Keralam government has released ₹88.23 crore to the bus operator KSRTC to cover revenue lost to the Priyadarshini free travel scheme, which 4,16,41,303 women passengers used from September 1 to September 30.
implications: Because the state reimburses the corporation, the cost of free travel is carried by the state budget rather than by the bus operator, so the scheme's scale becomes a recurring call on public money.
Women who travel on the free service could spend less on transport, which may leave more household income for other needs.

horizon.reason: Any effect on how colleges are inspected and on training quality would appear gradually, and the reports give no date for new arrangements.

items.headline: SC says internet access is a fundamental right, rejects blanket ban for children: ‘Safety and freedom are not at odds’
items.why: The Supreme Court has ruled that children have a fundamental right to access and use the internet and has rejected blanket bans. It has also barred online platforms from hosting subscription-based sexual content.

reports.headline: IndiaTech seeks rethink of turnover-linked gig worker social security levy
reports.summary: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, aggregators are required to contribute 1-2% of annual turnover towards social security for gig and platform workers, subject to a cap of 5% of the amount paid or payable to such workers.
